## ChatGPT's new rules come with bodyguards

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1672f514-1449-4471-9fb1-19e952d27f2a/Oct_30_-_1.jpg?t=1793350323)
Caption: 

OpenAI just [rewrote its Model Spec](https://openai.com/index/updated-model-spec/), the public rulebook for how ChatGPT should behave. It now focuses on five values: following human intent, minimizing harm, honesty, human agency, and care.

The company also revealed how it monitors its most powerful AI agents to catch suspicious behavior, including attempts to escape their testing environments.

* OpenAI replayed an earlier security incident and found that its new monitors would have raised an alert more than 30 hours before the actual breach.

* In a separate live training run, the monitors caught an AI model accessing the internet without permission within 15 minutes.

* Serious alerts go to human security teams, and some critical incidents can automatically pause the affected AI activity.

The 30-hour finding came from replaying an old incident, not catching it live.

OpenAI admits its models don't fully follow the new rulebook yet, and the monitoring system still has weaknesses. The company is writing rules for its AI while building ways to catch it when it breaks them.

81638.subject: Y Combinator Just Showed You What to Build. Here Are 33 Startup Ideas Worth Building Now 🚀
81638.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/yc-winter-2027-requests-for-startups

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
Y Combinator’s Winter 2027 Requests for Startups (RFS) opens with one sentence: “AI’s biggest bottlenecks are moving beyond the models.”
The 11 requests cover space access, the US robot supply chain, data center equipment, financing for physical AI, government benefits verification, city permitting, air-gapped AI, owned and vertical foundation models, AI-backed expert services and models that write well.
Read together, they make one argument. Intelligence is getting cheap. Steel, magnets, transformers, permits, verified data, capital and trust are not. YC is betting that the next cycle’s biggest companies will be built where AI runs into those constraints. The money already agrees. AI took $102B of the $159B in global venture funding in Q3 2026 (see below), and hyperscalers are on track to spend about $1T on capex this year.
The openings YC describes sit in the gaps around the companies raising $1 billion rounds: the actuator a humanoid maker can no longer import, or the Medicaid renewal a state can’t process by hand. Several of those gaps come with deadlines attached, and the first arrives in January 2027.
1. What changed in YC’s Winter 2027 RFS
From AI apps to AI bottlenecks
The previous list was still mostly about AI products. Fall 2026 included Multiplayer AI, a Cloud for Small Software, AI consumer products for a billion people, AI for the aging population, crypto, and Proving You’re Human.
Winter 2027 moves down the stack. Consumer apps are gone, apart from one request about how models write. And YC isn’t the only firm reading the market this way. In our breakdown of a16z’s State of Markets 2026 [ https://substack.com/redirect/dceb9821-2c45-47af-82e1-bcec846ea3d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], the firm traced the same rotation from bits to atoms and argued that supply-chain bottlenecks are where pricing power now sits.
The 11 requests sort into 5 themes:
The capital is already moving
Founder read: mega-rounds are going to a small number of companies. A capex boom this size also has a real financing problem, and the companies writing the checks won’t solve it for the suppliers and lenders around them.
Those numbers explain why YC wrote this list now. For each of the 11 requests, we checked YC’s claims against the latest data and paired them with three startup ideas you could start pitching this quarter.
Inside:
All 11 requests, broken down: what the YC partner behind each one wants, the market data that explains why now, and where the constraint moves next
